slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that make you
sound smarter instantly
Use precise words. Not "good" but "well organised" or "surprisingly funny." One precise word shows more intelligence than a long sentence full of vague ones.
Connect ideas from different fields. "That's a bit like how bees decide where to build a hive." Linking topics shows real thinking, not memorised facts.
Ask "why" before giving your opinion. Understanding someone's reasons before you answer makes your reply sharper and makes you look thoughtful and fair.
Feed your head a little every day. I do five minutes of history, art or science, and having real knowledge to draw on makes everything I say clearer and sharper.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Real knowledge to draw on makes everything I say clearer and sharper.

slides.texte_overlay: Explain complex things simply. If you can explain a big idea to a ten-year-old, people instantly see you understand it. Simple is the hardest form of smart.
Change your mind openly. "Good point, I hadn't thought of that." Updating your view when you hear a better argument is a sign of a strong mind, not a weak one.
Tell stories, not lists of facts. "In 1928, a scientist left a dish out by mistake..." A good story makes knowledge memorable and makes you worth listening to.
